claims.text: Register at stage-4 (lines 1-20): open debts N2 (old payments table left in donhang when Payments got its own database), N3 (POST /api/v1/orders accepts unitPriceVnd but ignores it), N4 (app hard-codes localhost); interest in words for N2 and N3 as stated.

Lines 24-29: hours so repayment is planned and weighed like a story; numbers are team assumptions, low-high as estimates not measurements; change counts are team guesses, change-hotspots.sh one source (history mostly lesson commits); no money, a team may multiply by its own hourly cost.

Lines 31-33: interest per quarter = changes to the area per quarter x extra hours per change; repaying pays off when interest summed over the time the area is still changed exceeds the principal; an area about to be removed is cheaper left as it is.

N2 (line 37): 2-4 changes/quarter, 1-3 extra hours each, interest 2-12 h/quarter, principal 6-10 h (drop table, remove from PostgresFixture, move or drop queries); at least 4 quarters because ADR 0028 and ADR 0031 touch it; 8-48 h over 4 quarters: pays off.

N3 (line 38): 2-3 changes, 0.25-0.5 h each, interest 0.5-1.5 h/quarter; principal 40-80 h (new API version without unitPriceVnd, /api/v2/orders request still carries it, move app, wait, retire old); many years, summed over 8 quarters: 4-12 h, below principal: accepted.

N3 row: revisit when /api/v1 has an end date, because the principal then is almost only the code change; the row gives no further reason. Interest unchanged: an end date does not change how often the order DTO is edited (reasoning, not in the register).

claims.text: N4 (line 39): 1-2 changes, 1-2 h each, interest 1-4 h/quarter, principal 16-24 h (read address from build-time configuration); 4 quarters 4-16 h, not yet paying off; interest rises sharply once the app runs on the cluster (every build for an environment must be edited); repay with that move.

Arithmetic from the table: N3's highest 8-quarter interest (12 h) is below its lowest principal (40 h); N2's lowest 4-quarter interest (8 h) is below its highest principal (10 h); principals order N3 > N4 > N2.

Register keeps interest in words (line 9, column 'Lãi mỗi lần sửa') and adds hours in a separate section (line 22); decision 'chấp nhận' = keep paying interest knowingly (lines 10-11); N1 is not in the hours table because it is repaid.

When the team must weigh repayment against stories, low-high hour ranges labelled as assumptions beat words only or one number; the repayment enters the plan as its own story or a stated share of each sprint, sized from the hours; words still say what the interest is.

claims.text: Choices: when /api/v1 gets an end date, recompute N3; before the app moves onto the cluster, re-estimate N4 and repay with the move; when leadership asks for money, give hours and let the team multiply by its own hourly cost.

Misconceptions: debt can be estimated in hours though not measured; a range is more honest than one exact number; the largest principal is not the most urgent (urgency = interest over time left vs principal).
